experiment.name: Forest Topology V3
experiment.purpose: Test whether correlation-derived non-contiguous Orange wedges concentrate terminal residual information better than contiguous Pine groups.

limitations: The same residual population was used for wedge construction and evaluation.
Per-item group selection is an oracle using actual residual energy.
Very low worst-case partial cosine values remain for some representations.
No quantization, production routing, serialization, or wall-clock retrieval is tested.

next_gate.hypothesis: Correlation-derived Orange wedges learned on training residuals retain their information-concentration advantage on unseen residuals.
protocol: split residuals into deterministic train/test folds
learn Orange grouping from training residuals only
retain oracle group selection for this gate only

supported: Correlation-derived non-contiguous groups have substantially higher within-group correlation than contiguous Pine groups.
Orange captures more terminal residual energy than Pine at every tested partial-access level.
Orange also beats deterministic random non-contiguous grouping.
The Orange advantage is therefore associated with learned representation structure rather than non-contiguity alone.
